---
title: "Sparse multinomial classification"
description: "Joint class probabilities, CLR coefficients and grouped predictor selection."
output: rmarkdown::html_document
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse=TRUE, comment="#>", message=FALSE, warning=FALSE)
library(L0glm)
options(width=90, digits=3)
```

For `K` categories the joint multinomial model uses the softmax probabilities

\[
\pi_{ik}=\frac{\exp(\eta_{ik})}{\sum_{h=1}^K\exp(\eta_{ih})}.
\]

`mgcv::multinom(K-1)` selects this family. The response can be a factor or a
matrix of category counts. Count rows may contain multiple trials.

## Fit and predict probabilities

```{r fit}
set.seed(22)
X <- matrix(rnorm(400*20), 400, 20)
eta <- cbind(1.2*X[, 1], -X[, 1]+X[, 5], -X[, 5])
prob <- exp(eta-apply(eta, 1, max)); prob <- prob/rowSums(prob)
y <- factor(vapply(seq_len(nrow(X)), function(i)
  sample.int(3, 1, prob=prob[i, ]), integer(1)), levels=1:3)

fit <- L0glm.fit(X, y, family=mgcv::multinom(K=2),
  lambda="gic", grouped=TRUE, relaxed=TRUE, maxit=150, tol=1e-8)
predict(fit, X[1:5, ], type="response")
```

## Interpret CLR coefficients

Adding the same constant to every class predictor leaves softmax probabilities
unchanged. L0glm reports centered-log-ratio (CLR) coefficients, with each row
summing to zero. A positive coefficient increases that category's log probability
relative to the geometric mean of category probabilities.

```{r clr}
coef(fit)[1:6, , drop=FALSE]
max(abs(rowSums(as.matrix(coef(fit)))))
```

`grouped=TRUE` selects whole predictor rows using class-symmetric row norms;
the model is fitted jointly. `grouped=FALSE` promotes sparsity in individual
displayed CLR entries, subject to their zero-sum constraint. Grouped relaxed
refitting admits all class coefficients in selected rows; ungrouped refitting
retains the selected CLR-entry pattern.

Explicit starting matrices are CLR-centered. Rows that are zero in every
channel are excluded in advance, with zero rows restored in the original output
dimensions; mandatory rows remain eligible. Scalar `start=1` centers to zero
in CLR space and does not lock out every predictor.

## Tune the grouped model

```{r tuning, eval=FALSE}
gic <- L0glm.tune(X, y, family=mgcv::multinom(2), tune="gic",
  nlambda=10, grouped=TRUE, relaxed=TRUE, maxit=150)
cv <- L0glm.tune(X, y, family=mgcv::multinom(2), tune="cv",
  nfolds=5, nlambda=10, grouped=TRUE, relaxed=TRUE, maxit=150)
predict(cv$fit_1se, X[1:5, ], type="response")
```

The [multinomial reference](../reference/L0glm_multinomial.html) gives the
joint IRLS equations and parameter counts. See also
[`mgcv::multinom()`](https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/mgcv/html/multinom.html)
for the family constructor.
